answers.rationale: Kara repeatedly prefers standard window seats on solo work trips and accepts an aisle only when a standard window is unavailable or the window costs an unjustified premium. A 90-minute same-terminal, carry-on connection does not create a meaningful need to prioritize the more-forward aisle seats. Restore the free windows on both flights.

Her normal seat instruction is to select a standard window when available, place a window request where the map cannot yet assign one, and use a check-in reminder to revisit unavailable seat maps. The 80-minute same-terminal connection with only a carry-on is not sufficient reason to override that preference for an aisle.

Kara consistently chooses a protected, reasonably timed return over a technically possible airport sprint, while also avoiding unnecessary late-evening travel for trivial savings. The 2:50 p.m. option costs only slightly more than the 11:20 a.m. flight but permits a normal post-teaching transition and hotel checkout; the 5:40 p.m. option wastes much of the afternoon and gets home later for little benefit.

With the lodge already checked out and the car packed Sunday night, there is no planned Monday activity that justifies paying more to depart three hours later. The 10:55 a.m. option is cheaper than the 1:55 p.m. option, gets them home much earlier for Tuesday work, and avoids the 10:40 p.m. arrival of the cheaper late option.
